mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 months, or the IC > 0.05 over the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: IC < 0.1 over 60-day horizon despite strong labor indicators, or SPX 60d returns are not statistically different from zero when labor signals are active.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) indicates weakening overall demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 3% from the previous month and HOUST falls by > 2%
failure_condition: 20-day IC over 5-day horizon remains positive, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production growth (INDPRO) above 2% monthly for three consecutive months suggests supply-side expansion that outpaces demand, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when INDPRO shows acceleration, or IC > 0.1 over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly increases by more than 0.5% in the month prior to the decision date during a tightening cycle, it signals future inflationary pressures that reduce equity valuation multiples and drive negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite the CPI surprise, or IC < 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market that can drive equity valuations up, producing positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases steadily for 4 consecutive months while PAYEMS remains flat
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly positive when labor indicators show tightening, or IC < 0.1 over the period.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a post-recession expansion phase characterized by rising industrial production (INDPRO), consumer confidence proxies (not available), and stable inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days regardless of trigger conditions.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain negative in multiple consecutive expansion regimes, or IC < 0.05 over 20 days during expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 2% for three months in a row during a low-rate environment, it creates accommodative conditions that boost risk sentiment and produce positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not positive when the low-rate condition persists, or IC < 0.05 over the horizon.
